key_insight: P2P is a phase 2A platform trial designed to efficiently evaluate multiple investigational therapies in early neuronal alpha-synuclein disease, not AI-driven cancer drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: The trial targets a biological disease continuum that can precede clinically manifest Parkinson’s disease; treatment benefits remain unproven.
method: Randomized, double-blind regimens assign 125 participants to active therapy and a variable number to placebo, with 96–144 weeks of treated follow-up.
Separate longitudinal Bayesian mixed-effects models evaluate DAT SPECT bilateral putamen binding and MDS-UPDRS Part III motor scores.
Analyses use shared placebo controls, dynamically discount controls from other regimens, and supplement estimates with nonrandomized PPMI cohort data.
evidence_signal: Endpoint selection drew on PPMI modeling and analyses, and simulations used longitudinal data from 275 P2P-eligible participants; the supplied abstract is truncated and reports no efficacy results.
watch_item: Borrowing shared and nonrandomized controls requires careful assessment of comparability to limit bias.
paper_title: Statistical design of Path to Prevention platform trial in early neuronal alpha-synuclein disease
